title: Evaluation of Prostate Artery Embolization Before Radiation Therapy for Prostate Cancer Treatment
official: Sequential Prostate Artery Embolization and Radiation Therapy Evaluation: SPARE
summary: This study will evaluate the safety of prostate artery embolization (PAE) before radiation therapy in men with localized prostate cancer who have an enlarged prostate and/or urinary symptoms related to benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). This study will evaluate the safety of this treatment approach and assess changes in prostate size, urinary symptoms, erectile function, and prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels. The study will also evaluate whether PAE may help some patients become eligible for stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) by reducing prostate size or improving urinary symptoms.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Men aged 18 or older
* ECOG ranging from 0 and 1
* Histologically confirmed intermediate risk prostate cancer per NCCN guidelines.
* Gland size 50 cc and over defined on MR prostate.
* Ability to undergo PAE.
* Ability to complete the PRO assessment surveys.
* Willingness to follow up after PAE.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Use of ADT.
* Prior history of focal therapy.
* Prior history of receiving pelvic radiotherapy.
* Patient with metastatic prostate cancer.
* Inability to undergo angiography.
* Severe atherosclerotic disease prohibitive of performing PAE.
* Severe contrast allergy.
* History of bladder neck or urethral stricture.
* Active urinary tract infection.
* Chronic prostatitis.
* Chronic pelvic pain.
sponsor: Weill Medical College of Cornell University
